questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question demonstrates end-to-end supply chain security expertise: image signing, SBOM provenance tracking, CVE scanning, and runtime verification in a multi-cloud, high-stakes environment. It tests knowledge of Sigstore ecosystem tools and policy enforcement.

- Image signing with Cosign/Sigstore for supply chain integrity
- CycloneDX SBOM generation for component transparency
- CVE scanning integration (e.g., Trivy, Snyk) for vulnerability detection
- Gatekeeper/OPA policy for runtime enforcement
- Canary deployments and rollback strategies in multi-cloud contexts

## Code Example

### GitHub Actions Workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yaml`)
```yaml
name: Image Provenance Gate
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  build-scan-sign:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }}
      
      - name: Generate CycloneDX SBOM
        uses: cyclonedx/ghcr-create-sbom@v1
        with:
          format: json
          output-file: sbom.json
      
      - name: Run CVE scan
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@master
        with:
          image-ref: 'ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }}'
          format: json
          exit-code: '1'
          severity: 'CRITICAL,HIGH'
      
      - name: Sign image with Cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3
        with:
          cosign-version: 'v2'
      - name: Sign image
        run: |
          cosign sign --yes ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }}
      
      - name: Generate SBOM with Syft
        run: |
          syft ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }} -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json
```

### Gatekeeper Policy (`constraint-template.yaml`)
```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: requirecosignsignature
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: RequireCosignSignature
      targets:
        - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
          rego: |
            package requirecosignsignature
            violation["image is not signed with Cosign"] {
              image := input.review.object.spec.containers[_].image
              notcosign.verify(image)
            }
```

### Failing Manifest (Unsigned Image)
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: unsigned-app
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: ghcr.io/org/app:unsigned-latest
    ports:
    - containerPort: 8080
```

### Passing Manifest (Signed Image)
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: signed-app
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: ghcr.io/org/app:v1.0.0
    ports:
    - containerPort: 8080
```

### Verification Steps
```bash
# Verify image signature
cosign verify ghcr.io/org/app:v1.0.0

# Verify SBOM exists
cosign verify-attestation --type cyclonedx ghcr.io/org/app:v1.0.0

# Verify against Gatekeeper policy
kubectl get requirecosignsignature
```

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests practical security controls: CI image signing, tag governance, and runtime enforcement with Kyverno; it requires understanding Cosign, Rekor, image verification, and policy-as-code interplay, plus how to craft minimal manifests and verify locally, in CI, and at runtime.

## Key Concepts

- Cosign signing and verification
- Tag policy regex
- Kyverno image verification at admission
- Minimal manifest testing (unsigned vs signed)
- CI and runtime integration and trade-offs (latency, private registries)

## Code Example

```yaml
# CI workflow snippet (Cosign verify)
name: CI Image Sign Check
on: pull_request
jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v1
      - name: Verify signatures
        run: |
          cosign verify registry.example.com/ride-service:1.0.0
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy (illustrative)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-signed-images
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: verify-signed-image
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    validateImages:
      - image: "*"
        cosign:
          publicKey: |
            -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----
            ...
            -----END PUBLIC KEY-----
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (unsigned image)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ride-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: ride
        image: registry.example.com/ride-service:1.0.0
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (signed image)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ride-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: ride
        image: registry.example.com/ride-service:1.0.0-signed
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle private registries and key rotation in Cosign?
- What are trade-offs of enforcing signatures at admission vs. build-time validations?
- How would you scale this policy across dozens of namespaces and clusters?

## Why This Is Asked

```rego
package main

deny[msg] {
  input.kind == "Deployment"
  some v in input.spec.template.spec.volumes
  v.hostPath != null
  msg = "hostPath volumes are forbidden"
}
deny[msg] {
  input.kind == "Deployment"
  cont := input.spec.template.spec.containers[_]
  cont.imagePullPolicy != "Always"
  msg = "imagePullPolicy must be Always"
}
deny[msg] {
  input.spec.template.spec.containers[_].securityContext.runAsNonRoot != true
  msg = "containers must run as non-root"
}
deny[msg] {
  input.spec.template.spec.containers[_].resources == null
  msg = "resources must be defined"
}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates expertise in policy-as-code across multi-cloud, multi-tenant ML infrastructure. It combines security hardening (image signing, secret management), resource governance (GPU quotas, container limits), network segmentation (default-deny policies), and operational reliability (canary deployments with SLO validation)—all critical for enterprise-grade ML platforms.

## Key Concepts

- **Policy Engines**: Kyverno and OPA Gatekeeper provide declarative, Kubernetes-native admission control
- **Image Signing**: Cosign ensures container image integrity and provenance verification
- **Secret Management**: ExternalSecret/SecretStore enables secure, dynamic secret injection from external stores
- **Resource Quotas**: ResourceQuota and LimitRange enforce compute, memory, and GPU allocation per tenant
- **Network Policies**: Namespace-scoped default-deny with per-tenant allow rules implements zero-trust networking
- **Canary/SLO Integration**: Prometheus metrics validate deployment health before traffic shifting
- **CI Integration**: Automated policy testing and manifest validation ensure consistent enforcement

## Code Example

```yaml
# Kyverno policy: require Cosign-signed images from approved registries
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-signed-images
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: check-signature
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Pod]
      verifyImages:
        - imageReferences:
            - "*.gcr.io/tenant-*/**"
          attestors:
            - entries:
                - keyless:
                    subject: "*@company.com"
```

## Why This Is Asked
Security hardening of Kubernetes manifests is a practical, repeatable gate in real projects. This tests understanding of policy-as-code, tooling choices (Kyverno vs Gatekeeper), constraint design for host access controls and image source controls, and CI integration in GitHub Actions with ephemeral test clusters.

## Key Concepts
- Policy-as-code with Kyverno or OPA Gatekeeper
- Constraints for host access (hostNetwork, hostPath, hostPort, privileged containers)
- Image source controls (allowed registries) and imagePullPolicy enforcement
- CI integration in GitHub Actions using KinD or similar ephemeral clusters

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-host-access
spec:
  rules:
  - name: block-host-network
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostNetwork is not allowed"
      pattern:
        spec:
          hostNetwork: "false"
  - name: block-host-path
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostPath volumes are not allowed"
      deny:
        conditions:
        - key: "{{ contains(element.volumes[].hostPath, '') }}"
          operator: "NotEqual"
          value: ""
```

## Minimal Policy (Combined)
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: security-guardrails
spec:
  rules:
  - name: deny-host-network-port
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostNetwork and hostPort are not permitted"
      pattern:
        spec:
          hostNetwork: "false"
          hostPort: "0"
  - name: deny-host-path
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostPath volumes are not permitted"
      deny:
        conditions:
        - key: "{{ @ }}"
          operator: "AnyNotIn"
          value: [""]
      foreach:
        - list: "spec.volumes[?hostPath]"
          deny: true
  - name: deny-privileged-containers
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "Privileged containers are not permitted"
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - securityContext:
              privileged: "false"
  - name: allowed-registries
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "Images must come from approved registries"
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - image: "registry.company.com/*"
            imagePullPolicy: "Always"
```

## Failing Manifest (hostPath + hostNetwork)
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: insecure-pod
spec:
  hostNetwork: true
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: docker.io/myapp:latest
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
    volumeMounts:
    - name: host-volume
      mountPath: /data
  volumes:
  - name: host-volume
    hostPath:
      path: /etc
```

## Passing Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secure-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: registry.company.com/myapp:v1.0
    imagePullPolicy: Always
```

## Local Validation
```bash
# Install Kyverno locally
```
